cases.question: Tell me about Pdfroo
cases.judge_reason: Answer correctly identifies Pdfroo as a client-side PDF editor with the right live URL, but adds many specific UI/UX details not present in the expected facts.
cases.answer:
**Pdfroo** is Ayush's fully client-side PDF editor — open a PDF, annotate, sign, rearrange/merge pages, and download a real flattened PDF. Nothing ever leaves the browser; all parsing, rendering, and writing happen locally via **pdf.js + pdf-lib**, and it works offline once loaded.

**Highlights**
- Runs on phones (375 px), tablets (768 px), and desktops (1440 px+) with mouse, pen, or touch
- No build step, no backend, no install — just open `index.html` or the live demo
- Thumbnail sidebar (desktop), slide-in drawer (tablet), bottom sheet (mobile)
- Drag-to-reorder pages (SortableJS, touch-friendly long-press on mobile)
- Rotate, duplicate, delete, insert blank pages, merge PDFs
- Find & replace, compress, and a "pouch promise" privacy notice
- Light/dark theme, local Fredoka/Nunito/Baloo 2 fonts, SVG kangaroo mascot
- After first successful download: a friendly kangaroo toast — "Done! Your PDF never left your device. Go enjoy a coffee ☕"

**Links**
- Live demo: https://ayush4u.github.io/pdfroo/
- Repo: https://github.com/ayush4u/pdfroo (MIT License)
